page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-2 is an entry-level compute-optimized virtual machine instance based on AMD EPYC 7B13 processors. The instance delivers two dedicated vCPUs mapped to one physical core with two execution threads on an x86_64 architecture. Hardware-level features include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 512 KB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, alongside instruction support for AVX, AES-NI, VAES, and SHA-NI. System memory totals 4.0 GB, yielding a 2:1 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. No local storage is bundled with the instance, requiring external network-attached block storage for persistent workloads, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provisioned by default. Dedicated GPUs or hardware accelerators are not included.

Benchmark results highlight solid single-threaded performance contrasted with limited parallel throughput due to the low core count. The instance achieves a strong stress-ng single-core score of 2,921.98, placing in the top 25 percent of tested systems, while its Geekbench single-core score lands in the middle tier at 1,612.0. However, multi-core benchmarks show sharp throughput constraints: multi-core stress-ng records 2,926.09, and Geekbench multi-core registers 2,013.0, placing in the bottom 10 percent. Memory bandwidth remains constrained, with large-block uncached reads measuring 31.59 GB/sec and writes at 23.42 GB/sec. Application tests reflect these limits, showing static web serving throughput of 2.82 GB/sec and Redis SET performance of 2.32 million operations per second.

From an architectural and cost-efficiency standpoint, c2d-highcpu-2 offers an affordable entry point for workloads that require dedicated compute cycles without paying for surplus memory or extensive multi-threading. The compact memory footprint and lack of bundled local storage limit its suitability for large databases, heavy build pipelines, or caching layers. It functions effectively for lightweight background microservices, modest API endpoints, single-threaded batch tasks, small-scale web serving, and basic continuous integration scripts.
